articles.title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant
articles.description: Kashim Chowdhury is accused of fraudulently juggling multiple public sector jobs.
articles.summary: Kashim Chowdhury wears dark sunglasses, a hat, hoody and gloves as he arrives at court.
key_points: A civil servant accused of fraudulently juggling multiple public sector jobs has told the court he "wasn't thinking straight" when he allegedly misled future bosses about his employment status.
Kashim Chowdhury said he was "in a panic" when he applied for a job at the Department of Health (DHSC), failing to declare he was already working at the Department for the Environment…
The prosecution said he already had three full-time jobs at the time, including roles at the London Borough of Tower Hamlets and East London NHS Trust.

articles.description: The bank says it is using more AI leading to a 5% reduction in its workforce.
articles.summary: Barclays is cutting around 5,000 staff as it introduces more artificial intelligence (AI) into its processes.
key_points: The banking group said 1,000 posts had already been closed and it expects a further reduction of 4,000 to be complete by the end of this year.
The cuts amount to 5% of its global workforce with most of them among operational and functional roles.
Barclays said the cuts were the result of investments in technology, with AI making some work processes more efficient.

articles.title: Tank barrel production returns to UK after 20 years
articles.description: The defence secretary says the UK is "back in the business of making weapons" for its armed forces.
articles.summary: Rheinmetall said the facility had created 100 jobs and it would look to expand its workforce in the future The production of gun barrels to be used on tanks has returned to the UK for the first time in 20 years with the opening of a new manufacturing facility.
key_points: The UK Gun Hall in Telford, run by German defence firm Rheinmetall, has supported 100 jobs and will make barrels and breaches for large calibre weapons.
Defence secretary, Wes Streeting, attended the opening ceremony on Thursday and said Britain was "back in the business of making weapons" for its armed forces.
"From an empty site to full production in eight months, this is rapid reindustrialisation in action," he said.

articles.title: Airbnb hosts can no longer make guests strip beds and wash dishes under new rules
articles.description: The updated policy will apply to all reservations booked on the accommodation site on or after 20 November.
articles.summary: Washing and putting away dishes are examples of chores that Airbnb says guests should generally not be asked to do Airbnb has changed its rules to limit what property hosts may ask guests to do - including when it comes to cleaning.
key_points: The updated guidelines state that hosts can now set seven standard house rules and can also add other "reasonable" requests.
Airbnb states that guests - who are required to pay a cleaning fee - should not be asked to complete tasks normally done by a cleaner, including washing dishes and stripping beds.
The new rules will apply to all reservations booked on or after 20 November on the accommodation marketplace.

Meta's head lawyer CJ Mahoney said the ruling made it "all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico".

articles.title: Burnham proposes plan to cut standing charges from gas bills
articles.description: The prime minister provided little detail, and there are questions over shifting the fees onto unit costs.
articles.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has asked ministers to develop a plan to remove standing charges from gas bills.
key_points: These are fixed daily fees that cover the costs of connecting to a supply.
They vary by region and households must still pay them even when energy is not being used.
Industry body Energy UK said whether the proposed changes would make a difference to bills would depend on how or where the charges were reallocated on the bill.

articles.title: Just Eat apologises for AI food mistakes after social media ridicule
articles.description: A spokesperson said it was removing inaccurate AI images and pausing the rollout of the tool.
articles.summary: A chip muffin and bacon and egg soda - menu items well known in parts of the UK, but not to the AI which made this Just Eat has apologised after it was ridiculed online over a series of mistakes with AI-generated pictures for some of its restaurants' food items.
key_points: The online food delivery platform had been testing out the tech to showcase food which didn't have images yet - but not all turned out as planned.
Instead the AI invented several bizarre concoctions, from bacon and eggs floating in a glass of cola - a confusion between "soda" and "soda bread" - to chips poking out of muffins.
A Just Eat spokesperson said the firm was "in the process of removing" the incorrect images, and would stop making more until the AI was further developed.

articles.title: Chocolate has a new problem. And it’s not cocoa prices
articles.description: Rising temperatures are reshaping the chocolate industry, impacting both cocoa supplies and consumer demand. As heatwaves become more frequent, manufacturers are adapting formats, product strategies and retail approaches to protect sales in a warming world.
articles.summary: Rapidly rising temperatures are reshaping the future of chocolate.
key_points: They’re impacting cocoa supplies, reducing crop yields and putting pressure on the world’s key growing regions.
But, not only that, they’re also impacting demand, as shoppers shift spending towards cool and refreshing alternatives.
The issue drew industry-wide attention when Lindt & Sprüngli cited it as a key factor in its decision to lower its 2026 growth forecast .

articles.title: UK beef, lamb, pork and dairy production to fall in 2027
articles.summary: The Agriculture and Horticulture Development Board (AHDB) has said that constrained cattle and sheep supply will remain a key feature of the market, underpinning market fundamentals in the years ahead.
key_points: Across the board, the levy body is expecting production of beef, lamb, pork and dairy to fall over the next year.

UK beef production, for example, is set to fall to 896,000 tonnes in 2027, marking a year-on-year decline of 0.8%, with increased carcass weights expected to only partially offset lower cattle throughputs.
The outlook for sheep is little better, with production forecast to decline by 2.4% to 262,000 tonnes in 2027 due to lower slaughter numbers and a contracting breeding flock.
